newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan is leader in UN race, France opposes him.
newsitem.headline: Annan is leader in UN race, France opposes him.

text.p: Kofi Annan of Ghana, the U.N. official in charge of peacekeeping, on Wednesday led four African candidates by a healthy margin in the race to become U.N secretary-general but France, which has veto power, continued to oppose him, diplomats said.
The envoys said that in the third of three Security Council ballots, Annan received 11 votes in favour and four against, one of them from France.
On Tuesday, Annan had received 10 favourable votes at the end of polling in the 15-member council, and was the only one of four African candidates to get more than the required nine votes.

At the end of Wednesday's voting, his closest rival was still Ivory Coast Foreign Minister Amara Essy, who had 6 votes in favour and 4 against, two of them presumably from the United States and Britain.

The spread between Annan and Essy was nearly the same in all ballotting on Tuesday and Wednesday, making Annan at this point the only viable candidate. In order to win, a nominee must have a minimum of nine votes and no veto.

France, the United States, Britain, Russia and China have veto power. The next round of balloting will be on Thursday and diplomats said the next step might be high-level discussions to persuade France to change its mind or possibly throw the race open to Asian nominess if the contest on African candidates is deadlocked.
Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, whose term expires on Dec. 31, has temporarily stepped aside in the race following a Nov. 19 U.S. veto of his candidature.
